#Figure 2
-----
```{r}
# Canonical exposure-category colors so a category is the same color everywhere
source("category_palette.R")
recolor_cat <- function(p) suppressMessages(
  p + scale_fill_manual(values = CATEGORY_PALETTE, na.value = "grey80") +
      scale_colour_manual(values = CATEGORY_PALETTE, na.value = "grey80"))
sum_yr               <- recolor_cat(sum_yr)
year_outcome_scatter <- recolor_cat(year_outcome_scatter)
vi_plot              <- recolor_cat(vi_plot)

# Education / race exposure-concentration panels (moved here from Figure 3)
# Both panels are CCREOH only -- the race/ethnicity categories (Creole,
# Hindustani, Javanese, Maroon) are Suriname-specific, so the generic titles
# read as though the panels were cross-cohort. Name the cohort in the title.
# Subtitle explains the median/IQR marks, which the panels carried unlabelled.
sdoh_marks <- "Points: participants. Dot: median. Thick bar: IQR. Thin bar: upper interval to Tau95."
edu_plot <- madres_plots[["CCREOH__Mat_Edu"]] +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.title.y = element_blank())+
    labs(color = "Education", subtitle = sdoh_marks) +
  ggtitle("Exposome Concentration by Maternal Education - CCREOH (Suriname)")
race_plot <- madres_plots[["CCREOH__Mat_Race"]] +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 16),
        axis.title.y = element_blank()) +
    labs(color = "Race/Ethnicity", subtitle = sdoh_marks) +
  ggtitle("Exposome Concentration by Race/Ethnicity - CCREOH (Suriname)")

fig2_patch <- sum_yr / (year_outcome_scatter  + mat_child_scatter) / vi_plot /
  edu_plot / race_plot


fig2_patch <- fig2_patch +
    # Panel A is a 4x4 facet grid; at 4/12 of the height its panels came out
    # ~4in wide by ~2.2in tall and the series read as squashed. 6/14 of a
    # taller canvas gives A about 4in per row while leaving B-F the same
    # absolute height they had before.
    plot_layout(heights = c(6, 2, 2, 2, 2)) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = 24), face = "bold")

ggsave(fig2_patch,file = "../../../Output/Paper1_Output_Submission2/Plots/Final_Patchplots/Figure2_All.pdf",height = 38,width =18)

```

#Figure 3
----
```{r}
# New Figure 3: 4-panel square of the cohort-heterogeneity / pooling story.
#   A = cohort effect spread by location   B = within vs naive-pooled decomposition
#   C = I^2 vs concentration divergence    D = between-cohort share of exposure
#                                              variance vs distortion from pooling
# (D was the budget-allocation simulation until 2026-08-10; see the note below.)
design <- "
AB
CD
"

pdf(file = "../../../Output/Paper1_Output_Submission2/Plots/Final_Patchplots/Figure3_All.pdf",height = 18,width =20)
# PANEL D SWAPPED 2026-08-10: was fig3_panels$cost (the fixed-budget allocation
# simulation), now fig3_panels$varshare (between-cohort share of exposure variance
# vs the distortion from pooling). The budget panel was the only non-empirical
# panel in Figure 3 and its ~25-cohort crossover is a property of the simulation's
# data-generating model, not of these cohorts; it now ships as
# Final_Patchplots/Supp_Pooling_Budget_Tradeoff.pdf. The new panel is empirical,
# is the mechanism behind A-C, and is estimable at two cohorts where panel B's
# ecological slope is not. See combined_realdata_figure.R section 2c.
# free(type = "label") on C and D, 2026-08-12. patchwork aligns axis TITLES
# across the whole layout, not just within a row. Panels A and B carry ~44
# y-axis rows of exposure-outcome names, so the title gutter for column 1 is as
# wide as those strings; C and D have short numeric ticks ("100", "0.3") and
# their y-titles were being pushed to the far left of that gutter, leaving a
# large empty band between the axis and its label. free() lets C and D place
# their own y-title next to their own axis while the PANELS stay aligned.
patch <- fig3_panels$spread + fig3_panels$decomp +
  free(fig3_panels$div + ggtitle("Heterogeneity and Concentration"),
       type = "label", side = "l") +
  free(fig3_panels$varshare + ggtitle("Effect Distortion and Exposure Variance"),
       type = "label", side = "l")
patch +
  plot_layout(design = design, heights = c(1.4, 1)) +
  plot_annotation(
  # Title changed 2026-08-10: "cost" referred to the fixed-budget simulation that
  # was panel D until that panel moved to supplementary. All four panels are now
  # diagnostic, so "consequences" is what the figure actually shows.
  title = 'Cross-cohort heterogeneity and the consequences of pooling associations',
  tag_levels = "A",
  # Sized above the 17pt panel titles so the figure title still reads as the
  # top of the hierarchy after the 2026-08-10 type scale-up.
  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 26, face = "bold", color = "#14213D"))
)   &
  # `face = "bold"` used to sit here as an argument to theme() rather than to
  # element_text(), where it did nothing. Folded into the element.
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = 28, face = "bold"))
dev.off()
```

source("../../../Coding/targeted_analyte_mapping.R")

mapping_path <- "../../../Input/Harmonized_Datasets/Targeted_Analyte_Category_Mapping.csv"
targeted_mapping <- read_targeted_analyte_mapping(mapping_path)

plot_categories <- c(
  "TraceElements", "Phenols", "Phthalates", "PAH", "PCB", "Parabens",
  "Smoking", "Pesticides", "VOCs", "FlameRetardants", "PFAS"
)

targeted_category_lookup <- targeted_mapping %>%
  dplyr::filter(Category %in% plot_categories) %>%
  dplyr::select(Code,Full_Name,CAS, Category) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()
